form.2. SHORT COURSE DESCRIPTION: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with increasingly capable coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes.
form.3. TOPICS / CONTENT AREAS:
Treatment of this list: starting hypotheses — may add/drop/reorder with justification
A. AI-Native Development: AI-assisted coding, coding agents, developer workflows

B. Agentic Software Engineering: MCP, agent skills, tool use, context engineering

C. Specification & Planning: spec-driven development, requirements to executable specifications

D. Software Development Workflows: loop engineering, iterative development, software factories

E. Engineering Practice: automated testing, evaluation, deployment, reliability

F. Practical Development: hands-on coding, projects, emerging developer tools
form.4. COURSE INTENT:
Central question the course answers: How can software developers effectively
design and operate development workflows in which humans and AI agents
collaboratively build reliable software?

Pedagogical emphasis: Practical, workflow-oriented understanding through
hands-on development and experimentation.

This course should NOT become:
- A general introduction to AI or machine learning
- A traditional programming course
- A purely theoretical treatment of large language models

familiarity with advanced programming and basic software engineering concepts.

project-based evaluation, and a final project.

existence.reason: While CSE701 covers aspects of AI in Software Engineering and has an overlap of 0.185, the new course focuses specifically on modern AI-native software development involving collaborative coding agents, workflow engineering, and agentic protocols rather than general mining of software repositories and empirical software engineering topics.
existence.recommendation: Proceed as a distinct elective course, serving as an advanced practical follow-on to core software engineering.

overlaps.differentiation: CSE701 focuses on broader research and mining techniques in software engineering using AI, whereas the new course centers directly on hands-on AI-native development workflows, agentic tool use, and loop engineering.
CSE581 covers traditional systems analysis and requirements engineering, whereas this course deals with spec-driven development and requirements translated for autonomous coding agents.
CSE582 addresses software product lines, evolution, and maintenance, while this course looks at modern software factories powered by AI coding agents.
CSE594A focuses generally on agentic reasoning for algorithmic and mathematical problem solving, whereas this course is specifically tailored to software engineering and coding workflows.
CSE201 teaches foundational advanced programming and unit testing in Java, while this course assumes those skills and builds automated testing and evaluation loops for AI agents.
AI501 provides a rigorous foundational treatment of machine learning theory and algorithms, whereas this course applies AI tools and agents within software engineering workflows.

prerequisites.justification: Students require solid software development fundamentals and unit testing knowledge to build reliable software and set up automated testing loops in AI-native workflows.

narrative.course_description: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes. The curriculum addresses AI-assisted coding and developer workflows, Model Context Protocol and tool use APIs, requirements engineering and specification-driven development, iterative loop engineering, and system assessment. Students will be able to configure AI-assisted coding tools, construct agent skills and Model Context Protocol integrations, decompose requirements into executable specifications, analyse iterative loop engineering workflows, and assess AI-native software development systems. The course is taught through a combination of lectures, tutorials, and practical laboratory sessions involving hands-on coding and projects.
narrative.sequencing_rationale: The modules progress from foundational AI-assisted coding and agent configuration through protocol integration and specification-driven development to iterative loop engineering and capstone system assessment. This sequence builds directly upon the software development and unit testing fundamentals established in prerequisite CSE201.
narrative.assessment_rationale: The assessment mix comprises quizzes, assignments, design documents, midsem examinations, and a project. This combination effectively evaluates both theoretical understanding and practical competency across all cognitive levels, ranging from configuration and code construction to comprehensive system design and live evaluation.
narrative.positioning_rationale: Unlike CSE701 which focuses on broader research and mining techniques in software engineering using AI, or CSE581 which covers traditional requirements engineering, this course centers directly on hands-on AI-native development workflows, agentic tool use, and loop engineering.
